steps.title: PHP susceptibility advisory - published 2026-10-21
steps.detail: PHP documents an unauthenticated pre-application mod_php demonstration and discusses other SAPIs with susceptibility qualifications. Broad web-serving risk attribution is not proof of equal demonstrated exploitability for every SAPI, configuration, version or patched installation.

steps.title: PHP request-state advisory - published 2026-10-21
steps.detail: The request-state advisory separates concrete demonstrations from candidate cases and configuration-dependent, same-worker request-state paths. Compare the cited SAPI and request prerequisites; this hub has not established them for any deployment.

steps.title: CISA conditional guidance - alert revised 2026-10-23
steps.detail: CISA advises temporary offline status when organizations cannot update immediately or continue using unsupported PHP 8.1 or earlier, until patched or updated. This is attributed guidance under those conditions, not a finding that every numerically older build is unpatched or unpatchable. The retained page does not establish its initial publication time.

steps.title: Separate PHP follow-up - notice published 2026-10-23
steps.detail: The initial-pair release list does not establish a fix for the later CVE-2026-115560. PHP described a next-regular-release plan and session.upload_progress.enabled=0 as an interim setting for an unusual path: php_binary or php_serialize switched to php through ini_set() before session_start(), with upload progress still enabled. That conditional measure is not complete mitigation of the initial pair. These sources do not establish a shipped third fix or historical CVE-registry absence.

cve_briefs.title: Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator advisory context

solutions.text: The recommended resolution is to upgrade to a fixed VCO release at your earliest convenience. These vulnerabilities have been fixed in the following releases: - VCO 5.2.3.18 and later in the 5.2 train - VCO 6.1.3.10 and later in the 6.1 train - VCO 6.4.2.12 and later in the 6.4 train

workarounds.text: Until the fixed software is deployed, operators should apply defense-in-depth controls appropriate for their environment: - Restrict access to the VCO web interface to trusted administrative networks. - Monitor the VCO for accesses from known malicious source IPs. - Monitor for unexpected outbound network activity from the VCO host. - Consider blocking outbound ports not needed for normal activities. - Monitor for backdoor daemons and webshells. - Review recent administrator activity for unexpected changes.

cve_briefs.required_action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

analysis.assessment: CISA records exploitation in the wild. Prioritize checking affected assets and the cited required action; this does not establish exposure on your devices.

contexts.label: SQL Injection

evidence.claim: The Related Attack Patterns table lists CAPEC-66 under CWE-89 and explicitly supplies its displayed pattern name.

contexts.label: Use After Free
contexts.definition_summary: Code accesses memory after it has been freed. If that storage is reallocated, an old pointer can refer into a new allocation where its original use is no longer valid.
contexts.definition_scope: Official catalogue definition only; not attack observation or window activity

evidence.claim: The captured official CWE page defines CWE-416: Code accesses memory after it has been freed. If that storage is reallocated, an old pointer can refer into a new allocation where its original use is no longer valid.

contexts.label: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
contexts.definition_summary: External input is incorporated into an SQL command without correctly neutralizing SQL-significant characters, allowing data to change the command interpreted downstream.

limitations: Late, partial saved-source subset; not an exhaustive incident, disclosure, exploitation or exposure census.
The fixed input generation is 5542 seconds before the nominal cutoff. Later capture, analysis and compilation do not reconstruct that missing tail.
Sixty undated and 3686 outside-period records are excluded. Date-only values use a declared UTC-calendar convention with unknown publisher timezone; none entered the main cohort.
All 148 selected exploitation fields remain unknown. Titles and CVE mentions do not establish exploitation, incidents, first disclosures or installed exposure.
Whole-input source health is 54 ok, 7 partial, 1 failed. The general CISA advisory collection failed; retained category-specific material does not establish full CISA coverage.
CVE-2026-104621, CVE-2026-104622 and CVE-2026-115560 failed enrichment and remain UNKNOWN; registry absence and shipped fixes are not established.
One entry title, one CNA title and four NGINX workaround/detail fields remain NULL. Withheld workaround text means unavailable, not no workaround.
Preserve product/version conditions, custom open bounds, distribution backports, PHP SAPI prerequisites and CVSS source/version. A version boundary alone does not verify a vendor package fix.
CWE/CAPEC mappings are taxonomy, not observed attacks. Publisher attribution and background do not establish actor identity or period activity.
The dedicated revision pass reconciled citation metadata only: zero new requests, article checks, comparisons or qualified baselines. Material changes are unknown.

Requested ten-minute collection after the saved 17:27 generation was not observed in bounded evidence. The last observed collection/deployment completed, but missing later freshness remains unresolved; this report does not claim it fixed.
Next nominal reporting/collection times are opportunities, not guarantees. Later refreshes cannot change this edition frozen input or counts.
